s1301.literal: Stone Classic Treatise in One Character, 1 scroll.
s1301.idiomatic: Stone Classic Treatise in One Character, 1 scroll.

s1302.literal: 三字Stone ClassicDocuments, 9 scrolls, Liang 有十三卷.
s1302.idiomatic: 三字Stone ClassicDocuments, 9 scrolls, Liang 有十三卷.

s1304.literal: 三字Stone ClassicSpring and Autumn, 3 scrolls, Liang 有十二卷.
s1304.idiomatic: 三字Stone ClassicSpring and Autumn, 3 scrolls, Liang 有十二卷.

s1305.literal: Above: 一百八部，四百四十七卷.
s1305.idiomatic: Above: 一百八部，四百四十七卷.

s1306.literal: Counting lost books together, 一百三十五部 titles, 五百六十九卷 scrolls.
s1306.idiomatic: Including lost books, totaling 一百三十五部 titles and 五百六十九卷 scrolls.

s1309.literal: If names are not correct, speech does not accord; if speech does not accord, affairs are not accomplished.
s1309.idiomatic: If names are not correct, speech does not accord; if speech does not accord, affairs are not accomplished.

s1310.literal: Expositors hold that writing arose from Yellow Emperor's Cang Jie.
s1310.idiomatic: Expositors hold that writing arose from Yellow Emperor's Cang Jie.

s1311.literal: Comparing categories and picturing forms is called wen; form and sound mutually enhancing is called zi; written on bamboo and silk is called shu.
s1311.idiomatic: Comparing categories and picturing forms is called wen; form and sound mutually enhancing is called zi; written on bamboo and silk is called shu.

s1312.literal: Hence there are the six categories: pictographs, phonetic compounds, combined meanings, explanatory transference, loan characters, and indicative forms.
s1312.idiomatic: Hence there are the six categories: pictographs, phonetic compounds, combined meanings, explanatory transference, loan characters, and indicative forms.

s1313.literal: In antiquity boys were shown things without deception; at six they were taught numbers and directional names.
s1313.idiomatic: In antiquity boys were shown things without deception; at six they were taught numbers and directional names.

s1314.literal: At ten they entered elementary school and learned writing and calculation.
s1314.idiomatic: At ten they entered elementary school and learned writing and calculation.

s1315.literal: At twenty they capped and began to study the Way of the earlier kings, and thus could complete their virtue and undertake affairs.
s1315.idiomatic: At twenty they capped and began to study the Way of the earlier kings, and thus could complete their virtue and undertake affairs.

s1316.literal: Yet from Cang Jie down to the beginning of Han, writing underwent five changes: first, ancient script, what Cang Jie created.
s1316.idiomatic: Yet from Cang Jie down to the beginning of Han, writing underwent five changes: first, ancient script, what Cang Jie created.

s1317.literal: Second, large seal script, what Scribe Zhou created in the time of King Xuan of Zhou.
s1317.idiomatic: Second, large seal script, what Scribe Zhou created in the time of King Xuan of Zhou.

s1318.literal: Third, small seal script, what Li Si created in Qin.
s1318.idiomatic: Third, small seal script, what Li Si created in Qin.

s1319.literal: Fourth, clerical script, what Cheng Miao created.
s1319.idiomatic: Fourth, clerical script, what Cheng Miao created.

s1320.literal: Fifth, cursive script, created at the beginning of Han.
s1320.idiomatic: Fifth, cursive script, created at the beginning of Han.

s1321.literal: When Qin abolished ancient script it first used eight styles: large seal, small seal, carved tally, seal impression, insect script, signature script, weapon script, and clerical script.
s1321.idiomatic: When Qin abolished ancient script it first used eight styles: large seal, small seal, carved tally, seal impression, insect script, signature script, weapon script, and clerical script.

s1322.literal: In Han the six styles were used to teach schoolboys: ancient script, odd characters, seal script, clerical script, twisted seal, and bird-and-insect—together with draft script, regular script, suspended needle, hanging dew, flying white, and more than twenty forms, all arising from the six scripts above and changing according to circumstance.
s1322.idiomatic: In Han the six styles were used to teach schoolboys: ancient script, odd characters, seal script, clerical script, twisted seal, and bird-and-insect—together with draft script, regular script, suspended needle, hanging dew, flying white, and more than twenty forms, all arising from the six scripts above and changing according to circumstance.

s1323.literal: 魏世又有八分Documents，其字義訓讀，有史籀篇、蒼頡篇、三蒼、埤蒼、廣蒼等諸篇章，訓詁、說文字林、音義、聲韻、體勢等諸Documents。.
s1323.idiomatic: 魏世又有八分Documents，其字義訓讀，有史籀篇、蒼頡篇、三蒼、埤蒼、廣蒼等諸篇章，訓詁、說文字林、音義、聲韻、體勢等諸Documents。.

s1324.literal: Afterward in Later Han Buddhist teaching spread in China and Western Region Kharosthi script was also obtained, able to cover all sounds with fourteen letters—text economical and meaning broad—called Brahmin script; its principle differs from the eight styles and six scripts, and is now appended under forms and styles.
s1324.idiomatic: Afterward in Later Han Buddhist teaching spread in China and Western Region Kharosthi script was also obtained, able to cover all sounds with fourteen letters—text economical and meaning broad—called Brahmin script; its principle differs from the eight styles and six scripts, and is now appended under forms and styles.

s1325.literal: Also when Later Wei first settled the Central Plains, military commands were all in barbarian speech; afterward influenced by Chinese custom, many could not be understood, so the original words were recorded and transmitted for teaching—called the "National Language"—now appended at the end of phonology.
s1325.idiomatic: Also when Later Wei first settled the Central Plains, military commands were all in barbarian speech; afterward influenced by Chinese custom, many could not be understood, so the original words were recorded and transmitted for teaching—called the "National Language"—now appended at the end of phonology.

s1326.literal: Also in Later Han the Seven Classics were carved on stone tablets, all written by Cai Yong.
s1326.idiomatic: Also in Later Han the Seven Classics were carved on stone tablets, all written by Cai Yong.

s1327.literal: In the Zhengshi era of Wei a three-script stone classic was also established; by transmission it was considered the correct characters of the Seven Classics.
s1327.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era of Wei a three-script stone classic was also established; by transmission it was considered the correct characters of the Seven Classics.

s1328.literal: At the end of Later Wei, when Qi Emperor Shenwu held power, they were moved from Luoyang to the capital at Ye; passing Heyang, the bank collapsed and they sank in the water.
s1328.idiomatic: At the end of Later Wei, when Qi Emperor Shenwu held power, they were moved from Luoyang to the capital at Ye; passing Heyang, the bank collapsed and they sank in the water.

s1329.literal: Of what reached Ye, not even half remained.
s1329.idiomatic: Of what reached Ye, not even half remained.

s1330.literal: In the sixth year of Kaihuang of Sui they were again carried from the capital at Ye into Chang'an and placed in the inner secretariat; it was proposed to repair and compile them and establish them in the National University.
s1330.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaihuang of Sui they were again carried from the capital at Ye into Chang'an and placed in the inner secretariat; it was proposed to repair and compile them and establish them in the National University.

s1331.literal: Soon afterward Sui fell into disorder and the matter was abandoned; the construction office used them as pillar bases.
s1331.idiomatic: Soon afterward Sui fell into disorder and the matter was abandoned; the construction office used them as pillar bases.

s1332.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Minister of the Secretariat Wei Zheng first gathered them together—not one in ten survived.
s1332.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Minister of the Secretariat Wei Zheng first gathered them together—not one in ten survived.

s1333.literal: Rubbing copies transmitted by inheritance still remain in the secret repository, together with the Qin emperor's carved stones, appended to this section to complete elementary learning.
s1333.idiomatic: Rubbing copies transmitted by inheritance still remain in the secret repository, together with the Qin emperor's carved stones, appended to this section to complete elementary learning.

s1334.literal: In all, the Six Arts classics and weft texts: six hundred twenty-seven titles, five thousand three hundred seventy-one scrolls.
s1334.idiomatic: In all, the Six Arts classics and weft texts: six hundred twenty-seven titles, five thousand three hundred seventy-one scrolls.

s1335.literal: Counting lost books together, 九百五十部 titles, 七千二百九十卷 scrolls.
s1335.idiomatic: Including lost books, totaling 九百五十部 titles and 七千二百九十卷 scrolls.

s1337.literal: If people do not study, they do not know the Way.
s1337.idiomatic: If people do not study, they do not know the Way.

s1338.literal: The gentlemen of antiquity were broadly learned without exhaustion, storing doubts to await questioning: learning did not overstep rank, teaching did not cross gradation;
s1338.idiomatic: The gentlemen of antiquity were broadly learned without exhaustion, storing doubts to await questioning: learning did not overstep rank, teaching did not cross gradation;

s1339.literal: words were concise and easy to understand, the teacher at ease and achievement doubled;
s1339.idiomatic: words were concise and easy to understand, the teacher at ease and achievement doubled;

s1340.literal: they both plowed and nurtured, and in three years completed one art.
s1340.idiomatic: they both plowed and nurtured, and in three years completed one art.

s1341.literal: From the time Confucius died and subtle words ceased, the seventy disciples passed away and the great meaning went astray; scholars lived apart in isolation, each forming a different doctrine.
s1341.idiomatic: From the time Confucius died and subtle words ceased, the seventy disciples passed away and the great meaning went astray. Scholars lived apart in isolation, each forming a different doctrine.

s1342.literal: Down to the Warring States, canonical texts were abandoned; Confucian scholars of the Six Classics could not exhaust their fundamental purport and mostly established minor techniques—a single classic reaching millions of words.
s1342.idiomatic: Down to the Warring States, canonical texts were abandoned; Confucian scholars of the Six Classics could not exhaust their fundamental purport and mostly established minor techniques—a single classic reaching millions of words.

s1343.literal: This caused scholars difficulty in understanding; they recited emptily in question and answer until lips rotted and teeth fell out without knowing benefit.
s1343.idiomatic: This caused scholars difficulty in understanding; they recited emptily in question and answer until lips rotted and teeth fell out without knowing benefit.

s1344.literal: The earlier kings established teaching to guard against human desire; it must be rooted in human affairs and broken at the mean.
s1344.idiomatic: The earlier kings established teaching to guard against human desire; it must be rooted in human affairs and broken at the mean.

s1345.literal: Heaven's command is brief and rarely spoken; principles outside the square were indeed not yet explained.
s1345.idiomatic: Heaven's command is brief and rarely spoken; principles outside the square were indeed not yet explained.

s1346.literal: By Later Han charts and prognostications were favored; in the Jin era abstruse talk was honored—boring through and fabricating, daily multiplying.
s1346.idiomatic: By Later Han charts and prognostications were favored; in the Jin era abstruse talk was honored—boring through and fabricating, daily multiplying.

s1347.literal: The correct canons of earlier kings were mixed with the delusive and false; discussions of great refinement were muddied with unrestrained extravagance.
s1347.idiomatic: The correct canons of earlier kings were mixed with the delusive and false; discussions of great refinement were muddied with unrestrained extravagance.

s1348.literal: Decline reached recent times; departure from the correct grew ever more distant, and there was no longer any method of teacher and precedent.
s1348.idiomatic: Decline reached recent times; departure from the correct grew ever more distant, and there was no longer any method of teacher and precedent.

s1349.literal: Study without understanding in the heart, exclusively honoring ornament and show; pre-fabricating mixed difficulties and posing them as adversarial pairs—thus there arose disputations of trimming corners, opposing sides, mutual following, and other competitive sophistries.
s1349.idiomatic: Study without understanding in the heart, exclusively honoring ornament and show; pre-fabricating mixed difficulties and posing them as adversarial pairs—thus there arose disputations of trimming corners, opposing sides, mutual following, and other competitive sophistries.

s1350.literal: Galloping in verbose speech to disorder canonical order, clamor becoming custom without knowing change—this is the blindness of scholars.
s1350.idiomatic: Galloping in verbose speech to disorder canonical order, clamor becoming custom without knowing change—this is the blindness of scholars.

s1351.literal: Ban Gu listed the Six Arts as nine categories, or with weft texts explaining the classics combined as ten categories.
s1351.idiomatic: Ban Gu listed the Six Arts as nine categories, or with weft texts explaining the classics combined as ten categories.
